about.title: About
about.intro: I'm a carpenter and computer scientist who builds things — in wood and in code. My work sits at the intersection of traditional craft and modern software engineering, where precision, patience, and a love for good systems apply equally.
about.carpentry.title: Carpentry
about.carpentry.desc: Furniture making, timber framing, and joinery using both hand tools and modern machinery. Each piece designed to last generations.
about.cs.title: Computer Science
about.cs.desc: Full-stack development, systems programming, and software architecture. Building tools that solve real problems in the workshop and beyond.
about.design.title: Design
about.design.desc: Both disciplines demand careful design before execution. Measure twice, cut once — whether in timber or in code.
about.tools.title: Tools
about.tools.desc: Hand planes, chisels, and mallets alongside Node.js, PostgreSQL, and a terminal. The right tool for the right job, always.
about.techNote: This portfolio is built with Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL + Vanilla JS · MVC + Component pattern
projectDetail.brandPara1: Every detail was approached with the same care applied across all work at Halli Smiley — whether hand-selecting timber grain for a cabinet face or architecting a database schema built to survive years of production traffic without a rewrite.
projectDetail.brandPara2: The result is a finished piece that balances function and aesthetic, built to outlast trends and hold up under real-world use.

adminBooks.vat.finding.ALREADY_FILED: A return for this period was already filed on {date}. A filed return cannot be changed — correct it through the next period, or re-open the period if it was not actually submitted.
adminBooks.vat.finding.UNPOSTED_DRAFTS: {count} journal entries are still drafts in this period. Draft entries are not part of the books, so their figures are missing from this return — and once posted they will land in whichever period is open then.
adminBooks.vat.finding.UNSUBSTANTIATED_I: {count} deductible purchases have no receipt attached, claiming {amount} of input VAT that cannot be proven. Attach the receipts, or mark the purchases non-deductible.

adminBooks.vat.finding.ZERO_RATED_NEEDS_: Box C reports {amount} of zero-rated turnover. Zero-rating must be supported by evidence of export, or of the customer being a business outside Iceland. Make sure that evidence is on file before filing.
adminBooks.vat.finding.REFUND_POSITION: This period claims a refund of {amount}. That is normal when input VAT exceeds output VAT — check it is what you expect.
adminBooks.vat.finding.NIL_RETURN: No VAT was recorded in this period at all. A nil return is still required, but check nothing is simply unentered.
adminBooks.vat.finding.PAST_DEADLINE: The filing deadline was {due_on}, {days} days ago.

adminBooks.payroll.title: Payroll
adminBooks.payroll.subtitle: Salaries, withholding tax and what is owed to Skatturinn.
adminBooks.payroll.bandsHint: Each band’s rate is the COMBINED income tax and municipal rate, exactly as Skatturinn publishes it. The municipal rate is not added again — it is shown here for reference only.
adminBooks.payroll.bandsFormHint: The lowest band must start at 0 kr. Enter the combined rate (income tax + municipal), not income tax alone — otherwise withholding comes out short by roughly a third.
adminBooks.payroll.needOneBand: At least one band is required.
adminBooks.payroll.refHint: RSK publishes these minimums every year. An owner who pays themselves below the minimum for their category has it assessed later, with interest.
adminBooks.payroll.noFiguresBody: The tax bands, personal allowance, social security and pension rates are set annually. Enter the year’s figures from Skatturinn’s published table before running payroll.
adminBooks.payroll.unconfirmedBody: Payroll will not compute anything until someone has checked the figures against Skatturinn’s published table. A run on unconfirmed figures produces a plausible amount that is too low — and the shortfall is the employer’s liability, not the employee’s.
adminBooks.payroll.confirmPrompt: Confirm the payroll figures for {year}? Write down where they came from — e.g. “skatturinn.is, checked 4 January”.
adminBooks.payroll.notePrompt: A note on where the figures came from is required.
adminBooks.payroll.yearFormHint: Every figure here is read off Skatturinn’s published table. Rates are entered as percentages (6.35 — not 0.0635).
adminBooks.payroll.saveUnconfirms: Editing the figures clears the confirmation — they need checking again.
adminBooks.payroll.figuresSaved: Figures saved. Confirm them before running payroll.
adminBooks.payroll.owedHint: Read from the ledger, not from the payroll runs — only the books know whether the remittance has actually gone out.
adminBooks.payroll.name: Name
adminBooks.payroll.overrideHint: A blank pension rate means “use the year’s minimum” — which is not the same as 0. A collective agreement may be more generous than the minimum, never less.
adminBooks.payroll.ownerHint: An owner needs a reference wage category, so the minimum salary can be checked.
adminBooks.payroll.draftHint: A draft computes payslips but posts nothing. The tax year comes from the PAY DATE — December’s salary paid in January is taxed on January’s figures.
adminBooks.payroll.draftedWithBlockers: Draft computed, but {count} thing(s) block posting.
adminBooks.payroll.confirmPost: Post the payroll? This creates a liability to Skatturinn and cannot be deleted — only reversed.
adminBooks.payroll.postedOverridden: Payroll posted, with the reason recorded.
adminBooks.payroll.overridePrompt: Post anyway? Write the reason — it is stored with the run.
adminBooks.payroll.reversePrompt: Reverse this payroll run? Nothing is deleted — a mirror entry is posted. Why?
adminBooks.payroll.payPrompt: How much was paid? {amount} is outstanding.
adminBooks.payroll.badAmount: The amount must be a whole number greater than zero.
adminBooks.payroll.employerCost: Total employer cost: {amount} — the gross plus social security and the employer’s pension contribution.
adminBooks.pos.title: Counter sales
adminBooks.pos.subtitle: Over-the-counter sales — receipt, VAT and posting in one go.
adminBooks.pos.productNoRate: {name} has no VAT rate. Set it on the product — the till does not guess.
adminBooks.pos.freeLineHint: For a repair, a delivery charge, or anything that is not a shop product. The VAT rate is required — a till cannot ask.
adminBooks.pos.badPrice: The price must be a whole number greater than zero.
adminBooks.pos.emptyBasket: Nothing on the counter yet. Pick a product to start.
adminBooks.pos.buyerHint: A receipt does not need a name. A business buyer does need their kennitala on it, to deduct the input VAT.
adminBooks.pos.cashHint: {count} sales — this should be in the drawer
adminBooks.pos.cardHint: {count} sales — awaiting settlement from the acquirer
adminBooks.pos.creditedHint: Money that went back out — not netted off the sale, because the sale happened.
adminBooks.pos.vatHint: VAT is extracted from the price, not added to it. Shop prices include VAT.
